prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- “Secure future” built on lower taxes, controlled migration, strong defence, and reformed public services. Contrasts plan with Labour on taxes, spending and borders.

Economy, tax and business
- Fiscal rules maintained; debt to fall in target year. At least £6bn/year from tackling avoidance.
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament. No rise in income tax or VAT.
- Maintain National Living Wage at two‑thirds of median earnings (c.£13/hour on forecasts).
- Pro‑SME agenda (business rates reliefs, prompt payment, finance access, cut reporting burdens); no rise in corporation tax; keep key investment reliefs; explore full expensing for leasing when affordable.
- Major infrastructure from HS2 savings; nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in populated areas. Rail reform via Great British Railways.

Families, childcare and welfare
- 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school; expand Family Hubs to all LAs.
- Child Benefit moved to household basis: taper from £120k to £160k combined income.
- Welfare reform: tighten PIP and Work Capability Assessments; overhaul fit notes to work/health specialists; tougher sanctions after 12 months; expand UC; new Fraud Bill.

Pensions
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and create age‑related tax‑free allowance to keep pension below tax threshold. No new pension taxes; maintain lump sum and marginal rate relief.

Education, skills and youth
- Advanced British Standard (English and maths to 18); expand academies; parent right to see teaching materials; statutory school mobile phone ban; two hours PE weekly.
- 100,000 extra apprenticeships funded by closing low‑value degrees; Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: competitive paid military/cyber year or 25 days civic service.

Borders, migration and security
- Legal annual cap on migration (work/family) that falls each year; higher salary thresholds; health checks and higher IHS; visa fee rises.
- “Stop the boats”: monthly removals to Rwanda; implement Illegal Migration Act; reform asylum rules internationally; more returns deals.
- Defence to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn for munitions; scale defence R&D; strong Ukraine support; Veterans’ Bill and benefits.

Health and social care
- NHS funding rise above inflation; recruit 92k nurses/28k doctors; Pharmacy First; 50 new Community Diagnostic Centres; 40 hospitals by 2030.
- £3.4bn NHS tech plan (App as front door, AI, faster imaging, federated data); productivity target 1.9% p.a.
- Dental recovery (2.5m more appointments; NHS service tie‑in for new dentists).
- Women’s Health Strategy; expand mental health support in schools/communities.
- Implement Cass Review; define biological sex in Equality Act; protect single‑sex spaces; ban private puberty blockers.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes: brownfield fast‑track; higher urban densities; lift “nutrient neutrality” with mitigation fees; development corporations.
- Help to Buy relaunch (5% deposit, 20% equity loan); permanent FTB Stamp Duty threshold £425k; mortgage guarantee continues.
- Leasehold reform; renters’ reform (abolish Section 21 after court changes); CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; tougher sentences; Martyn’s Law.

Energy, net zero and environment
- Net zero 2050 with “pragmatic” approach: no new green levies; lower bill levies; maintain price cap; review standing charges.
- Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; triple offshore wind; expand CCS; scale nuclear (SMRs, Wylfa); import carbon pricing by 2027.
- £6bn for home efficiency plus universal vouchers; protect best farmland from solar; no fracking.
- +£1bn farming budget; legally binding food security target; seasonal visas tapered; renew £100m Seafood Fund.
- Plan for Water: tougher penalties, executive bonus bans for serious breaches; river recovery network; extend SW water rebate.
- Tree planting/peat, new National Park, 15‑minute access to nature; tougher fly‑tipping and waste crime.

Transport, drivers and culture
- Backing Drivers Bill: ban local road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; referendums for 20mph/LTNs; extend £2 bus fare for Parliament; no new smart motorways.
- Independent Football Regulator; support women’s sport; creative sector tax incentives; BBC funding review; uphold press freedom.

Union and devolution
- Protect internal market; direct levelling up funds UK‑wide; investment zones/freeports; targeted commitments for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
